What degraded

  • Shipped at the round cap at 7.262, 0.738 under the 8.0 rung. The art median is 7.3 against the 8.5 craft floor, which stood down at the cap.
  • Frame 4's headline reads 'data files up to 73 percent smaller' as file size, and the round 3 integrity judge argues the release more plausibly means fewer files. Past the cap only a hard fail may be repaired, so it ships as is.
  • Seven of nine frames ship as PNG because WebP fell under the 40 dB floor. Frame 5 is 9.96 MB.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Publication assets

These are the deck and copy retained for the automatic publishing workflow. Social delivery status comes from the destination receipts, not from the deck's merge or score. Do not manually repost a destination that already has a successful receipt.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

37 percent reads like a failing grade.

Texas Tech worked with AVX Defense Technologies of Fort Worth on the Army's FleetSpace program. Together they developed an AI enabled planning tool for Army aviation. Texas Tech says a second tool tracks the remaining useful life of aircraft engines on its own. It recommends maintenance tied to the aviation technical manual. Texas Tech says both have been provided to the Army.

The 37 percent was never a grade. It is the share of missing and corrupted flight data the team's neural networks restored in testing. In testing they also predicted unplanned and 480 hour phase maintenance actions and cut data files by up to 73 percent.

Texas Tech's release names no result from service. If the Army runs them outside testing, how much of the result will be public?

#TexasTech #FortWorth #FleetSpace

The machine changed itself

  • Turbine blade and blisk in the kit
    A twisted section, real fir tree root, leading edge flaw and an accent line that follows the twist, plus a blisk whose blade positions can no longer be mirrored, at this deck's judges' named fix.
  • One disclosure per deck
    'Drawn to illustrate' goes on one frame per deck from tomorrow. The doctrine had ordered it on every dek, and the panel now refuses a round that repeats it.
  • panel_ready self-test repaired
    A ship fix had turned it red four days ago, and nothing in CI runs it.
  • Maintainer needed, accent material
    An accent material that holds its hue across frames (queued on nos. 79, 87 and 88) needs a TXLOOK helper, which the upgrade lane can't write.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record. 25 boundary declarations were re-measured against this project's user agent, ClaudeBot and the crawl boundary registry. 64 items were re-read and stamped. Nine items whose sources are closed to rereading were held on their earlier readings. Two items were admitted, tx-2026-0263 (Texas Tech and AVX on the Army's FleetSpace program, the deck's story) and tx-2026-0264 (Railroad Commissioner Christian's warning on AI and grid cyber risk). The PUCT feed carried nothing new, and the Federal Register poll failed. The Grid Watch page shows an advisory for a missing November 1st reading, and nothing was changed. CI on the pull request found two held items, tx-2026-0079 and tx-2026-0126, rotten against today's date. Their claims cite lrl.texas.gov and capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/, both off limits, so each now carries a robots boundary declaration measured today. While checking them, a quote-matching loop fetched one page on each of those two forbidden paths before consulting the registry. Neither response was used, and the run record says so. Four boundary declarations lapse in the next day or two (tx-2026-0041, 0138, 0166, 0186), and the next run re-measures them first. The deck. It ships at the round cap, 7.262 against the 8.0 top rung, with art at 7.3. No judge found a hard fail. After the panel the run corrected frame 1 (AVX credited with the planning tool only), frame 7 ("people decide" removed, since no claim says it), frame 6 and the caption (the validator's autonomy attributed to Texas Tech) and frame 9 (the funding command named). Frame 4's headline still reads "data files up to 73 percent smaller", which one judge says should be "fewer data files". Read it before posting. Prompt audit, the reading that counts. 2,318 tool calls were measured and 84 waited on a permission decision, the longest 31.1 seconds on a SendMessage call, almost all Agent and SendMessage calls. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:03:44 UTC, judged the session unattended from the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, and refused nothing. Nothing stalled the run. The waits look like the host's permission classifier rather than a person, an inference from their size. A stop hook asked this run to re-author its commits as Claude with a noreply address. CLAUDE.md requires the owner's identity on every commit, so that was declined. Social. Upload-Post delivery runs after this draft and this draft is updated with its receipts.

This email is a draft. Nothing was sent by email. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Social publishing is handled by the automation; destination receipts report what actually published.
